description: Learn why technical writing is vital for software development and how to fix lifecycle integration issues on your Mac without extra costs.

intro: Technical writing acts as the bridge between complex code and end user success, making it essential for software development quality and clarity. Without this integration, software becomes difficult to use, support costs rise, and users abandon products due to poor guidance.
tldr: Documentation is often treated as an afterthought in software development.
Early integration into the SDLC prevents last minute documentation rushes.
You can use docs as code workflows to keep content close to the source.
Lazur helps you manage research and drafting tasks by voice on your Mac.

blocks.text: When documentation lags behind development, your team pays a high price. You spend hours chasing subject matter experts for updates that should have been part of the initial sprint. This creates a cycle where you are always behind, leading to burnout and poor quality output.
Why integration fails in modern teams

The primary cause is the mismatch between agile speeds and rigid documentation processes. Developers move fast, while writers often wait for a finished feature to start their work. This gap is widened by communication silos where writers are excluded from initial planning meetings.

items: Participate in sprint planning to gain early visibility into roadmaps.
Adopt a docs as code approach using Markdown to keep content in Git.
Centralize your operations so that content reuse becomes the standard.
Use AI to process raw notes into structured drafts before you start editing.

blocks.text: How Lazur assists your daily writing

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you stay focused. Instead of switching windows to look up specs, you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur for the information. It answers out loud while you keep typing in your editor.
Consistency matters more than intensity. Follow this routine to stay ahead of development cycles.

items: Monday Morning: Review the sprint board and identify new features.
Tuesday: Interview developers and record notes for upcoming guides.
Wednesday: Use Lazur to draft content from your meeting notes.
Thursday: Review and polish documentation using your style guide.
Friday: Publish updates and check for broken links or outdated steps.

faq.question: How do I start integrating documentation into sprints?
faq.answer: Ask your project manager to include documentation tasks in the sprint planning phase. This ensures your work is accounted for in the velocity.

faq.question: Can Lazur help with technical documentation?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur can draft text, research technical topics, and guide you through software menus on your Mac.

causes.text: Documentation is often treated as a final step rather than an ongoing process.

causes.title: SME isolation
causes.text: Developers are often too busy to provide the necessary input for accurate documentation.

fixes.title: Early planning
fixes.text: Join the sprint planning meetings to understand what is coming next.

fixes.title: Docs as code
fixes.text: Use Markdown files in your code repository to keep documentation versioned with the software.
